summary: Helen Baroni is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She studied at Grinnell College, Princeton Theological Seminary, and Columbia University under Paul B. Watt. In 1993, she took up a post at the University of Hawaiʻi.

Helen Hardacre specializes in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Vanderbilt and the University of Chicago under Joseph M. Kitagawa and Jonathan Z. Smith, she held posts at Princeton, Griffith University, Harvard University, and the Reischauer Institute.

Helen Wang specializes in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She studied at SOAS University of London (1984–1988) and became Curator of East Asian Money at the British Museum around 1993.
Helena Blankleder is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under traditional teachers Pema Wangyal Rinpoche and Jigme Khyentse Rinpoche, as attested in 1999.
Helena Michie studied at the University of Pennsylvania from 1979 to 1984. She held an academic post at Rice University around 1990.

Helga Uebach was a scholar of Tibetology and Indology. She completed her PhD at the University of Munich (~1961–1967) and joined the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 1964 as a research associate.
Hellfried Dahlmann was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He held academic posts at the University of Marburg (~1936–1952) and the University of Cologne (~1952–1973).

Sinologist Hellmut Wilhelm earned his doctorate at Humboldt University of Berlin under Otto Franke after studies at Frankfurt, Kiel, and Grenoble. He held posts at Peking University (~1933–1948) and the University of Washington (1948–1971), and co-edited Monumenta Serica.

Hellmuth Hecker was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Hamburg (PhD ~1946–1948) and under Paul Debes. From approximately 1953 to 1988, he served as a referent at the Forschungsstelle für Völkerrecht und Ausländisches Öffentliches Recht.

Helmer Smith was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Uppsala University and under Richard Pischel and Karl Friedrich Geldner. He held posts at Lund University (1921) and Uppsala University (1936–1947).

Helmut Eimer was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin, the University of Hamburg, and the University of Bonn under Frank-Richard Hamm, later serving on Bonn's faculty (~1975–2001).

Helmut Hoffmann specialized in Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Berlin (PhD under Heinrich Lüders) and Marburg. Hoffmann held positions at the Prussian Academy, the Ahnenerbe, Hamburg, the University of Munich, and Indiana University.

Helmut Krasser was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He completed his Promotion and Habilitation at the University of Vienna, where he taught (~1988–2007), and led the Austrian Academy of Sciences' Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

Helmut Rix was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Würzburg, Heidelberg (PhD 1950), and Tübingen (Habilitation ~1959). He held posts at Tübingen, Augustana-Hochschule Neuendettelsau, the University of Regensburg, and the University of Freiburg (1982–1993).

Helmut Tauscher is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Ernst Steinkellner. He has held positions as a professor at the University of Vienna (attested 2010–2015) and as a Numata visiting professor at Leiden University.

Helmuth von Glasenapp worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, completing a doctorate under Hermann Jacobi at Bonn. He served as a lecturer at Berlin and Bonn, then held chairs at the universities of Königsberg (1928–1944) and Tübingen (1946–1959).

Helwig Schmidt-Glintzer is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Göttingen (~1967–1968) and the University of Munich (~1968–1972), later holding professorships at Munich (~1981–1993) and Göttingen (~1993–2013).

Henepola Gunaratana is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied in Sri Lanka and earned a PhD at American University. He served at the Buddhist Institute of Kuala Lumpur, Washington Buddhist Vihara, American University, and Georgetown University.

Heng Sure is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Oakland University, UC Berkeley, and the Graduate Theological Union under Ronald Y. Nakasone and Hsuan Hua, he has taught at the Graduate Theological Union, Dharma Realm Buddhist University, and Bond University.

Henk Blezer specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He completed his degrees at Leiden University, where he subsequently held posts as a postdoctoral researcher (1993–1997) and teacher (2002–2008), alongside an affiliation with the International Institute for Asian Studies (1997–2001).
